deities: Guru Padmasambhava (eight incarnations in fierce form depicted)
Zangdok Palri (Guru Rinpoche's heavenly palace) - seven-tiered painted wooden model on the top floor, built by the late Dungzin Rinpoche over five years
festivals: Chaam (monastic mask dance) - 28th and 29th day of the 12th Tibetan month (February/March) - the monastery's main annual festival

history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy); originally a small lhakhang enlarged during the reign of the third Chogyal Chakdor Namgyal, who was regarded as the third reincarnation of Lhatsun Chempo, Jigme Pawo
history.period: Early modern - planned, designed and founded by Lama Lhatsun Chempo in 1705; one of the oldest and premier monasteries of Sikkim

name: Pemayangtse Monastery
town: Pelling (CSV town 'Pemayangtse' is the monastery's own name, not a town)
town_description: Pelling, at about 2,150 m in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, is Sikkim's premier hill resort town with close views of Kanchenjunga. Nearby attractions include the Pemayangtse Monastery, the ruins of Rabdentse (the old Sikkimese capital), Sanga Choeling Monastery, Khecheopalri Lake and Darap village.
tradition: Tibetan Buddhism (Nyingma) - NOT a Hindu temple

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 130-160 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 130-150 km (verify).
travel.road: About 2 km from the Upper Pelling football ground; reachable by taxi or shared jeep from Pelling or Geyzing (Gyalshing).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear Himalayan views; February-March for the Chaam dance festival (dates follow the Tibetan calendar).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Monastery visiting hours typically 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (verify); photography rules inside the shrine hall vary (verify).
